VERDICT: The claimed same-assumption \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(n)\)-delay theorem is not currently supported. Injective uncertain-edge gadgets can canonicalize within-core directed-Steiner witnesses, and a least-index core rule can remove equal completed outputs, but neither prevents exponentially many per-core minima that strictly contain an obstruction from another core.

CONSTRUCTION OR WALL: For a completed set \(X\), global minimality and ownership are inexpensive: test each core’s feasibility inside \(X\), reject \(X\) if any core is feasible inside \(X\setminus\{x\}\) for some \(x\in X\), and otherwise assign \(X\) to the least feasible core. This works only at leaves. Pruning a partial support requires deciding whether it has a completion containing no already-known obstruction \(B_i\); the constraints \(B_i\nsubseteq X\) are equivalently \((U\setminus X)\cap B_i\neq\varnothing\) for every \(i\), i.e. a hypergraph-transversal constraint coupled to existential reachability/group choices. The cited group-Steiner reduction shows that this is a genuine dualization barrier, while bounded \(b\) supplies no bounded incidence-treewidth hypothesis. No NP-hardness proof for this exact parameterized extension test is established here, but assuming it polynomial/FPT would simply assume the missing theorem. The unconditional bound is therefore candidate-sensitive total time—polynomial/FPT work per raw per-core minimum—with potentially exponential delay between global outputs.
